# React 19 API Changes

Covers dimension 1: new hooks, Actions, Server Components, ref-as-prop, metadata, stylesheets.

For source details, see [citations.md](../citations.md).

## New Hooks

| Hook | Import | Purpose | Key Behavior |
|------|--------|---------|-------------|
| `use(resource)` | `react` | Read Promises and Context during render | Can be called conditionally (breaks traditional hook rules); suspends on pending Promises [1][11] |
| `useActionState(fn, init, permalink?)` | `react` | Manage async action state | Returns `[state, dispatchAction, isPending]`; replaces deprecated `useFormState` [1][12] |
| `useOptimistic(currentValue)` | `react` | Show optimistic UI updates | Immediately renders optimistic value; reverts on error [1] |
| `useFormStatus()` | `react-dom` | Read parent `<form>` status | Returns `{pending, data, method, action}`; must be called from child component [1][38] |
| `useDeferredValue(value, initialValue?)` | `react` | Enhanced with `initialValue` option | Returns `initialValue` on first render, schedules re-render with deferred value [1] |

### React 19.2 Additions (October 2025)

| Hook | Import | Purpose |
|------|--------|---------|
| `useEffectEvent(fn)` | `react` | Separate "event" logic from Effect logic; always sees latest props/state [4] |

### use() — Breaking the Rules of Hooks

The `use()` hook is the first hook that can be called conditionally — inside `if` statements and `for` loops [1][11]. Unlike `useContext`, it can read context after early returns. Key constraints:

- Cannot be called in try-catch blocks (use Error Boundary instead) [11]
- Server Components should prefer `async/await` over `use()` [11]
- Promises passed from Server Components are preferred (stable across re-renders) [11]

### useActionState — Replacing useFormState

Key differences from `useReducer` [12]:

| Aspect | useReducer | useActionState |
|--------|-----------|----------------|
| Side effects | Must be sync, pure | Can be async, perform side effects |
| isPending | Not provided | Built-in |
| StrictMode | Invoked twice | NOT invoked twice |
| Action execution | Immediate | Wrapped in Transition |

Actions are queued sequentially — each receives the previous call's return value as `previousState` [12].

## Actions System

Actions are functions using async transitions [1]. They provide:

- Automatic pending state management
- Optimistic updates via `useOptimistic`
- Error handling with Error Boundary integration
- Automatic form reset on success for uncontrolled components
- Sequential request handling

### Form Actions

```jsx
<form action={actionFunction}>
  <input type="text" name="name" />
  <button type="submit">Update</button>
</form>
```

The `action` and `formAction` props work on `<form>`, `<input>`, and `<button>` [1]. Manual reset available via `requestFormReset()` API [1].

## Component & Ref Improvements

### ref as Prop

Function components now accept `ref` directly as a prop [1][2][24]:

```jsx
// New — React 19
function MyInput({placeholder, ref}) {
  return <input ref={ref} />;
}

// Old — forwardRef (deprecated)
const MyInput = forwardRef(({placeholder}, ref) => (
  <input ref={ref} />
));
```

Does not apply to class components (refs reference instances) [1].

### Ref Cleanup Functions

Refs can now return cleanup functions, called on unmount [1]:

```jsx
<input ref={(ref) => {
  // setup
  return () => { /* cleanup */ };
}} />
```

**Breaking change:** TypeScript now rejects implicit returns from ref callbacks. Fix: use explicit block body [2].

### Context as Provider

```jsx
// New
<ThemeContext value="dark">{children}</ThemeContext>

// Old (still works, deprecated in future)
<ThemeContext.Provider value="dark">{children}</ThemeContext.Provider>
```

Codemod available [1][28].

## Document & Resource Management

### Document Metadata

`<title>`, `<meta>`, and `<link>` tags automatically hoisted to `<head>` when rendered in components [1]:

```jsx
function BlogPost({post}) {
  return (
    <article>
      <title>{post.title}</title>
      <meta name="author" content="Josh" />
      <link rel="author" href="https://twitter.com/joshcstory/" />
      <h1>{post.title}</h1>
    </article>
  );
}
```

Works with client-only apps, streaming SSR, and Server Components [1].

### Stylesheet Support

Automatic DOM insertion order management based on `precedence` attribute [1]:

```jsx
<link rel="stylesheet" href="foo" precedence="default" />
<link rel="stylesheet" href="bar" precedence="high" />
```

External stylesheets load before revealing dependent content. Deduplicates across renders [1].

### Resource Preloading APIs

| API | Purpose |
|-----|---------|
| `prefetchDNS(url)` | DNS lookup only [1][40] |
| `preconnect(url)` | Establish connection [1] |
| `preload(url, {as})` | Download resource without executing [1][39] |
| `preinit(url, {as})` | Download and execute [1] |

All imported from `react-dom` [1].

### Async Script Support

`<script async={true} src="..." />` can be rendered anywhere in the component tree, deduplicates across components [1].

## Server-Side Features

### Server Components

Stable in React 19 [1][36]. Key caveats:

- Bundler/framework APIs are **not semver-stable** in React 19.x minors [1][36]
- Framework authors should pin to specific React version or use Canary [1]
- "use server" directive is for Server Actions, not Server Components [1]

### React 19.2 Additions

- **`<Activity>`** component: visible/hidden modes for pre-rendering [4]
- **`cacheSignal()`**: cleanup/abort for cache() lifetime in RSC [4]
- **Partial pre-rendering**: `prerender()` + `resume()` APIs [4]
- **Batching Suspense boundary reveals** for SSR [4]

## Error Handling Improvements

### Consolidated Error Logging

React 19 eliminates duplicate error logs [1][2]:

- Previously: 3 error logs per caught error
- Now: single consolidated log with full context

### New Root Options

```js
createRoot(container, {
  onCaughtError: (error, errorInfo) => {},   // Error Boundary caught
  onUncaughtError: (error, errorInfo) => {}, // Not caught
  onRecoverableError: (error, errorInfo) => {} // Auto-recovered
});
```

Uncaught errors report to `window.reportError` instead of multiple console logs [2].

### Hydration Error Diffs

Single error message with visual diff showing server vs client mismatch [1].

## Custom Elements

Full support — passes all tests on Custom Elements Everywhere [1][42]:

- SSR: primitives render as attributes; non-primitives and `false` omitted
- CSR: props matching element properties assigned as properties, others as attributes

## Suspense Behavior Change

React 19 changed Suspense sibling behavior: siblings of a suspended component are no longer pre-rendered [17]. This creates waterfall fetching instead of parallel fetching for siblings in the same Suspense boundary.

Workaround: render-as-you-fetch pattern — preload data before component renders [17].

The React team postponed the v19 release after community feedback at React Summit (June 2024) and committed to a compromise solution [17].

## Static Rendering APIs

New `prerender()` and `prerenderToNodeStream()` APIs wait for all data before returning HTML stream [1].

## Gaps and Limitations

- Exact Suspense waterfall behavior fix status needs verification against final React 19.0 release
- Custom elements property detection algorithm details not fully documented
- Resource preloading browser compatibility matrix not published
- `useFormStatus` behavior across portals and Suspense boundaries not documented
